dataset.title: Reviews
dataset.description: One row per review. status is OK when the row carries a review, FILTERED_OUT when the reviews were read but your own publishedAfter or language removed all of them (free), NO_REVIEWS when the profile is open and the pages asked had nothing (free), or NOT_CHECKED_* with the reason in plain words: INVALID (the line is not a domain, or the stars filter is not a rating from 1 to 5), DUPLICATE (the same company came earlier), LIMIT (beyond maxCompanies), NOT_FOUND (Trustpilot has no profile at that domain, HTTP 404), BLOCKED_PAGE (a bot wall answered instead of the listing), HTTP_ERROR (4xx or 5xx), and TIME, CAP, BILLING or ERROR when the run stopped. TIME, CAP and ERROR also mark reviews that were read and not delivered, because a read review is never dropped in silence. A review row carries: company (the Trustpilot identifying name), companyDisplayName, companyTrustScore, companyReviewsTotal, reviewId, url, rating, title, text, language, author, authorCountry, authorReviews, verified, publishedDate, experiencedDate, companyReply and companyReplyDate, starBucket (1 to 5, or null for the newest unfiltered page), starSource (newest or star-filter), input and inputIndex (the line it belongs to). billable is a claim about the price list; the money actually taken is chargedEvents in the summary.

summary.title: Run summary
summary.description: Run summary. companiesRequested always equals companiesAttempted plus companiesNotAttempted (invalid, duplicate, limited, skipped before the run reached them). Companies that were attempted end in exactly one of companiesRead, companiesNotFound, companiesBlocked, companiesNoReviews, companiesFilteredOut, companiesFailed; companiesPartial marks a company whose reviews were read and then the listing stopped answering. reviewsSeen counts every review the pages carried, reviewsUnique drops the repeats between pages and star buckets, reviewsDelivered counts the rows written, and chargedEvents is the money really taken. reviewsFiltered and reviewsLimited were read and not charged; reviewsLimited splits into reviewsCapped, reviewsStopped and reviewsUncertain. deliveredUncharged is a batch that is in the dataset and was not paid for, chargeUncertain is a batch whose fate is unknown: it may be in the dataset and it may be uncharged. byStatus splits the rows by status. pagesFetched and pagePlan show the pages read and the pages intended. browserMode (headful under Xvfb is the mode that passes the wall), pricingEventPriced, billingActive and pricingNote say how the run stood with the price; null there means the price could not be read, not that billing is off. starBuckets, starBucketsFromPage, maxReviewsPerCompany, maxPagesPerCompany, maxCompanies, publishedAfter and language echo the settings actually applied. reviewsBucketMismatch counts reviews that a star listing answered with a rating it does not carry: they are dropped, never charged, and the company gets its own row naming the reason. counterMismatch is true when the numbers above do not add up, so a wrong count is never silent. stopReason names why the run stopped early, and an empty stopReason means it finished the list.
